title: Lumping Unrelated Domain Concepts "Because Their Fields Match"
pattern: Unifying distinct domain concepts into a single type simply because they share the same primitive fields (e.g., amount, date, description).
why_bad: The concepts are "false cognates" — they appear similar structurally but have entirely separate rules, lifecycles, and reasons for change. Merging them forces developer teams to step on each other's validation logic, leading to fragile designs.
detection: A single struct representing multiple distinct business classifications that do not share common lifecycles or business rules.
counterexample: Pure, raw value structures (like `Money`) that are completely devoid of business identity.
source: *Domain-Driven Design* (Evans), Chapter 14: "duplicate concepts and false cognates", p. 407.
